_README: THE SCORING MODEL. Edit this file, not the score.
Every item is one concrete deliverable with a WEIGHT in body-of-work units
(roughly: how much of this project's effort it is/was) and a VALUE in 0..1.
A section's score is the weighted mean of its items. The overall score is the
An item's value comes from exactly one of two places, and the difference is
the whole point of this file:
"value": n      -- ATTESTED. A human confirmed it. `evidence` must say how.
"probe": "..."  -- MEASURED. score.py computes it from the tree every run.
⚠ THE ONE RULE: never raise an attested value because something LOOKS done.
Raise it when a run on real hardware confirmed it, and put the run in
`evidence`. This project's most expensive bugs have all been things that
read as working -- see docs/STATE.md, `a stepped-over call still answers`.
⚠ THE BAR IS 'ntvdm SUPERSET ON XP-32', ONE BAR, FOR EVERY SECTION. It is NOT
the DOS games bar. Doom and Skyroads being playable is two items here, not a
score of 85. Scoring the halves against different bars is how the 2026-09-04
review got a headline of 65 that its own components did not support.

#133 CLOSED s52 -- oracle, rig AND stock ntvdm agree on all six cases. #131 STILL NOT CLOSED, but s54 turned it from a blocked decision into a LOCATED BUG. (1) THE RECORDED HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED: `we are a GUI-subsystem binary where stock ntvdm is console` is simply false -- our PE subsystem is already CUI, pinned deliberately in CMakeLists.txt. (2) A FIFTH ROUTE was tried and eliminated: VDM_COMMAND_INFO carries StdIn/StdOut/StdErr at +0x10, which is how stock gets a console it never inherited; ours come back as non-handles (0x02341fc0/0x7c867f23/0x65470000, identical every run, all three FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN). (3) THE INSTRUMENT THAT SAID SO NAMED THE REAL DEFECT: the WHOLE struct is junk -- CreationFlags 0x4d445674 and CodePage 0x78654e74 are ASCII and constant, AppName is garbage, TaskId is 0 -- so GetNextVDMCommand returns TRUE and populates NOTHING. We never noticed because the launch does not depend on it (the program comes from target.txt or our own command line). And the command line says why: it arrives as `-f` with NO -i<taskid>, so CSRSS cannot tell which queued task we are asking about. The shape that DOES carry -i (anything through `start`, which is every run rt.bat has ever done) reports TaskId 0x18 and gets `inherited console` -- which is exactly how this stayed invisible for fifty sessions. ==> #131 IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE M2.5 ITEM `recover the real command line from CSRSS's undocumented multi-call protocol`; fixing one fixes both. (4) AND THE TARGET IS PROVEN REACHABLE, by the oracle rather than by argument: `hello.com > out.txt` typed at cmd writes 136 bytes under STOCK ntvdm on the same box and 0 bytes under ours. Live streaming is wired and works the moment a handle exists; what is missing is the handshake, not the plumbing.

#47 s53 CLOSED ON HARDWARE: every figure is right and every row self-consistent -- Conventional 639K = 4K + 635K, Upper 0K, Reserved 0K, Extended (XMS) 16,384K = 0K + 16,384K, Total under 1 MB 639K, Largest executable 635K (650,240 bytes). ★ AND THE SHAPE MATCHES THE 6.22 ORACLE ROW FOR ROW (`./scripts/oracle.sh --batch MEM`): same seven rows, same labels; the numbers differ honestly (our resident DOS is 4K where 6.22`s is 19K). ROOT CAUSE was a SECOND absolute-offset read, the same class as the first: MEM asks AH=52h for SysVars, KEEPS THE SEGMENT, THROWS THE OFFSET AWAY and reads <SysVars segment>:0x008C as the conventional/upper line (mem.exe image 0F88/0F8E/0F95, bucketed at 0x1304 and 0x31DB). We left it ZERO, so every segment compared >= 0 and the WHOLE CHAIN was filed as upper -- the phantom 1,663K with our real free block inside it. 6.22 has 0xFFFF there, and it was in the lolprobe dump already on disk. GAPS, neither a figure: we say `The high memory area is not available` where 6.22 says MS-DOS is resident in it (true -- we provide no HMA); `MEM /C` and `MEM /D` are unverified.

CLOSED s53, rig-gated and diffed against stock. ROOT CAUSE: MS Paint takes the mouse capture on button-down and NEVER gives it back -- nine SetCapture and ZERO ReleaseCapture in one measured session, and it RE-TAKES it after every button-up. That is legal Win16, but USER32 refuses SC_KEYMENU while the calling thread holds a capture (menus deliberately do not open mid-drag), so DefWindowProc did nothing with Alt and the menu bar was dead for the rest of the session. ★ THE FIX IS WHAT STOCK IS OBSERVED TO DO, not an invention: cross-process GetGUIThreadInfo (new `rigshot capture` verb) shows stock ALSO leaves the capture on the canvas after three drags, and Alt MOVES it to the top-level window and enters GUI_INMENUMODE. We now do the same on WM_SYSKEYDOWN for VK_MENU/VK_F10, and only when one of OUR windows holds it. ★ WHY STOCK GETS IT FREE: its thread reports GUI_16BITTASK (flags 0x20), ours reports 0 -- USER32 gives its own WOW threads special menu handling and that flag is not settable from outside. VERIFIED: after three canvas drags, menuowner set and flags=0x04 (GUI_INMENUMODE), and the File menu is open in the screenshot with the drawn stroke visible behind it -- docs/research/evidence/session53-menu-after-drags.png.

#136 s53/s54, RIG-GATED on 192.168.1.29: 24 of 47 rows are live, up from 7. s54 ADDS THE ONE THE OLD NOTE CALLED OUT BY NAME -- `the whole CPU page needs a duty-cycle throttle on the exec loop (there are no cycles to count on a real CPU)`. SpeedMode is no longer the dead DOSBox-vocabulary combo (Auto|Maximum|Fixed cycles); it is the approximate-speed dropdown of GH #56, Unlimited|200|100|66|33|16|8 MHz, on the Settings CPU page AND as a radio submenu under Machine, both backed by one registry value. Old values migrate: index 0 meant `do nothing` before and still does. MECHANISM: the exec thread is SUSPENDED for a share of each period -- the same SuspendThread/GetThreadContext/ResumeThread machinery async_inject_irq has used for twenty sessions -- gated on g_in_exec so a lock holder can never be stopped; the mode-12h interpreter paces itself by instruction budget instead. MEASURED ON HARDWARE, four sweeps of tools/dostest/cpubench.asm (a loop costing 12 cycles on a 486, so MHz comes from a period CPU's published timings rather than a guess): unthrottled 3665 MHz apparent; 100 MHz -> 103 measured; 200 -> 305; 66 -> 89; 33 -> 73; and the two slowest SATURATE, which the host LOGS as delivered_mhz beside the requested one rather than pretending. 36 new off-VM checks. THREE MECHANISMS WERE MEASURED WRONG BEFORE THIS ONE WAS RIGHT, and each was wrong in a way that looked like success: a per-millisecond Bresenham gave 6x where 87x was asked (the Suspend/Resume cost ate each 1 ms hold); sleeping the off-period whether or not the hold LANDED let the guest run free half the time and made the sweep NON-MONOTONIC; and pricing the hold off the 1 ms we ASK for rather than the run phase actually measured came out 3.5x fast at every setting. Selftest stays 8/8 and at Unlimited every throttle counter reads zero, so the default is the old behaviour exactly. GAPS: CpuType/CpuCore/Fpu/Cycles/Turbo are still scaffold; ConventionalKB/Umb need DOS_MEM_TOP to stop being a compile-time constant; Renderer needs a windowed DirectDraw blit that does not exist; Opl needs an OPL3 that does not exist. And the honest cost: a slow setting is CHUNKY -- 1 ms of running per ~110 ms held at 33 MHz -- because 1 ms is the smallest unit Sleep can hand out. NOT YET USER-JUDGED: whether the five speed-affected demos FEEL period-correct, which is #56's own acceptance bar and needs eyes on the box. CAVE was launched and left running for that; note it is the VSYNC-paced one, so MATRIX_1 (delay-loop) and BUBBLES (unpaced) are the sharper tests.

#130 s52: target.txt no longer overrides unconditionally. ★ s53 THE INSTALL/UNINSTALL FLOW IS NOW VERIFIED ON HARDWARE, AND BEHAVIOURALLY RATHER THAN BY THE REGISTRY VALUE -- a key that reads correctly and does not route is the failure this project has been bitten by. installcycle.bat: (1) delete the Debugger value, run a DOS program -> NO host log, so stock ran it; (2) add the value back, run THE SAME program -> host log present, so ours ran it; (3) delete and re-add, proving the key each time. That is the stated gap closed. ★ AND WIN16 COVERAGE IS 9 GUESTS, NOT 5: NOTEPAD, PBRUSH, SYSEDIT, SOL, WINMINE, CLOCK, RECORDER, CHARMAP, MPLAYER have all been routed through the IFEO hook and put a window on the desktop this session; five are user-confirmed doing their job. GAP, and it is why this is 0.8 and not 1.0: there is still no INSTALLER -- installing means `reg add` by hand, and a product needs a command or a UI that does it, checks for an existing value, and can put it back

CLOCK.EXE.note: s53 LAUNCHES: real 336x361 window with its Settings menu; all 5 missing services implemented (GDI ExtTextOut + 4 USER) and neneeds reports 0 to do. Its ExtTextOut calls arrive with correct digit rects and return drawn. NOT done: THE FACE IS BLANK, and the shape is now pinned even though the cause is not. In 18 s: 19,929 WM_PAINT, 9,964 InvalidateRect(NULL, erase) -- EXACTLY ONE PER PAINT -- 9,964 BeginPaint/EndPaint, 69,745 GetSysColor, and only 50 WM_TIMER. So it is a paint->invalidate->paint loop at ~555/s, not a timer-driven redraw, and the drawing is erased faster than it lands. ⚠ AND IT NEVER CALLS GetCurrentTime (0 calls), so the time it compares against comes from krnl386 16-bit code reading the BDA tick with NO THUNK TO OBSERVE. ▶ NEXT STEP: instrument the BDA tick RATE AS THE GUEST SEES IT -- if it advances faster than 18.2 Hz, Clock believes the time changed on every idle pass, which is exactly this loop
